No one approves their own entry
Year-end entries need the Chief Financial Officer
Revenue only from pay applications and the schedule
Adopted by the board March 31, 2025. Demonstration document; every name and figure is invented.
Who may post. The Controller and the Project Accountant post manual journal entries. Subledger entries are posted by the people who run each subledger.
Review. Manual journal entries over $25,000 are reviewed and initialed by a second person before posting: the Controller for others’ entries and the Chief Financial Officer for the Controller’s own.
No one approves an entry they prepared.
Support. Every manual journal entry has its support attached in the system or filed in the month’s close binder: the schedule, invoice, contract or calculation it comes from.
Year-end entries. Entries posted after the June subledgers close need written support and the Chief Financial Officer’s approval, whoever prepares them.
Revenue. Contract revenue is recorded from pay applications and the quarterly contract schedule (over and under billings). Revenue is not recorded by any other manual entry.
Closing. When a month is closed the Controller locks the period. The year is closed when the board accepts the year-end trial balance.
Reversals. Accruals are marked to reverse on the first day of the next period.
